url-shortener.intro: Design a URL shortening service like bit.ly. Users submit a long URL and receive a short link that redirects to it. Start by clarifying the requirements: what must it do, and roughly how much traffic should it handle?

REQUIREMENTS.followUp: Good. Redirects will dominate writes by orders of magnitude — what latency target would you commit to for a redirect, and why?
REQUIREMENTS.challenge: You haven't addressed {gap}. How does it shape the design before you draw any boxes?

COMPONENTS.followUp: Hashing the long URL versus handing out counter-based keys — which did you pick, and what does the other one buy you?
COMPONENTS.challenge: There is no {gap} in your design yet. What fails without it at the traffic you estimated?

DATA_MODEL.followUp: The access pattern is essentially a point lookup by key. Does that change your storage choice? What would a relational store give you that you'd be giving up?
DATA_MODEL.challenge: You skipped {gap}. Sketch it — what columns or fields, and which one do lookups hit?

SCALING.followUp: Suppose a single short link goes viral and receives 30% of all traffic. Which component saturates first, and what's your mitigation?
SCALING.challenge: Push further on {gap} — at 10x the traffic you estimated, what breaks and how would you address it?

rate-limiter.intro: Design a distributed rate limiter that protects an API from clients exceeding their allowed request rate. Start with requirements: what are we limiting, at what granularity, and how strict must enforcement be?

concepts.label: limit granularity (per user / IP / API key)

REQUIREMENTS.followUp: If the limiter itself becomes unavailable, should requests fail open or fail closed? Defend it.
REQUIREMENTS.challenge: You haven't pinned down {gap}. Without it, how would you know whether a burst is acceptable?

concepts.label: algorithm choice (token bucket / sliding window / leaky bucket)

COMPONENTS.followUp: Fixed windows allow 2x bursts at the boundary. Does your algorithm have that problem? What does fixing it cost in memory?
COMPONENTS.challenge: Your design has no clear {gap}. Where does it live and what does the request path look like?

DATA_MODEL.followUp: Two limiter instances read the counter at the same instant, both see 99 of 100, and both allow. How do you prevent that — and is preventing it worth the latency?
DATA_MODEL.challenge: Address {gap}. How much memory per client does your state take at the scale you estimated?

SCALING.followUp: A single abusive client sends 1M requests/second. Does the limiter itself survive, or does it become the bottleneck?
SCALING.challenge: Dig into {gap}. What's the concrete failure mode at 10x scale and your mitigation?

chat-application.intro: Design a real-time chat application like WhatsApp or Slack supporting one-to-one and group messaging. Start with requirements: message delivery guarantees, online presence, and expected scale.

REQUIREMENTS.followUp: Is it acceptable for two members of a group to see messages in different orders? What does strict ordering cost?
REQUIREMENTS.challenge: You haven't covered {gap}. How does it change what 'correct' means for this system?

COMPONENTS.followUp: Users A and B are connected to different chat servers. Walk the message from A's socket to B's socket — every hop.
COMPONENTS.challenge: There's no {gap} yet. What breaks for a user whose phone is asleep?

DATA_MODEL.followUp: How do you page through message history efficiently, and what's your partition key so a hot group doesn't hit one node?
DATA_MODEL.challenge: You didn't address {gap}. How will a client fetch the last 50 messages of a conversation?

SCALING.followUp: A 100k-member group sends one message. What is the write amplification, and where would you cut it?
SCALING.challenge: Go deeper on {gap}. What's the failure at 10x scale and how do you contain it?

news-feed.intro: Design a social news feed like Facebook's or Twitter's home timeline. Users follow others and see a ranked, near-real-time feed of their posts. Begin with requirements and scale assumptions.

REQUIREMENTS.followUp: Is a feed that is 30 seconds stale acceptable? What product features become impossible if you answer yes?
REQUIREMENTS.challenge: You haven't discussed {gap}. It determines whether you precompute feeds or build them on read — settle it first.

concepts.label: fan-out on write vs fan-out on read

COMPONENTS.followUp: A celebrity with 50M followers posts. Under pure fan-out on write, what happens, and what's your hybrid?
COMPONENTS.challenge: You have no explicit {gap}. Without it, where does a new post go the instant it's published?

DATA_MODEL.followUp: Do you store full posts in each follower's timeline or only ids? What does each choice cost on read and on edit/delete?
DATA_MODEL.challenge: Spell out {gap}. What are the fields and which access pattern is it optimised for?

SCALING.followUp: A post is deleted after it has been fanned out to 2M timelines. How does your system stop showing it, and how fast?
SCALING.challenge: Push on {gap}. At 10x the scale you assumed, what saturates and what's the fix?
